title: Do You Have Enemies?
body:
As Christians, we have enemies, both physical and spiritual. Even when things are going well for us, and we are experiencing the mighty blessings of God, Satan is there, somewhere in the background, walking about "seeking whom he may devour". (1 Peter 5:8)

Sometimes he uses people. "For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ". (Philippians 3:18)

Psalm 58 is one of many imprecatory Psalms, and reminds us we can, and should, deal with the enemy. Even in the good times.

Prepare for the Enemy (v1-5)

Expect the enemy to be:

Unrighteous and Unjust (v1)

Heartless and Violent (v2)

Wicked from the womb (v3)

Speaking lies (v3)

Poisonous, dangerous, and out of control (v4-5)

Pray Against the Enemy (v6-8)

Pray their Power will be Disabled (v6)

Pray their Plans will be Disappointed (v7)

Pray their Purpose will be Destroyed (v8)

Perceive the Ultimate Destruction of the Enemy (v9-11)

Their destruction comes quickly and surely. (v9)

Their destruction comes with God's wrath. (v9)

Their destruction comes with God's vengeance. (v10)

Their destruction comes with God's righteous judgement. (v11)

How to destroy an enemy:
"Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good." (Romans 12:20-21)

If you are living as an enemy of God, God's people desire you to be saved from the wrath and judgement that is sure to come.

That is also God's desire for you!

"Much more then, being now justified by his (Jesus) blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life." (Romans 5:9-10)

title: Are You an Enemy of God?
body:
In the midst of writing about his rejoicing and joy concerning the type of church the Thessalonians had become, the Apostle Paul turned his thoughts to the enemies of the church in 1 Thessalonians 2:15-16.

#1. They Fight the Power of God (v15)

They killed the Lord Jesus

They killed the prophets

They persecuted the apostles

Stephen spoke to them this way in Acts 7:51-52: "Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye. Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom you have been now the betrayers and murderers:" Six verses later they stoned him to death.

Lost people today are not just fighting the people of God, but they are fighting the very Power of God those people represent! Power that is mighty to save!

Are you fighting God's power? "ye do always resist the Holy Ghost"

#2. They Forbid the Word of God (v16a)

"that they might be saved"

"But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name." (John 20:31)

Most lost folks today are not forbidding the Word of God from being preached, but they all ARE forbidding the Word of God from taking root in their heart so that they might be saved.

Are you forbidding God's Word to have its effectual work in your life?

#3. They Fill Up Their Sin Against God (v16b)

"to fill up their sins alway"

As Jesus spoke to the Jews, "Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do..." (John 8:44)

In Genesis 15:16 God noted to Abraham that "the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full". But eventually their iniquity (sin) caught up with them.
God is "not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance." (2 Peter 3:9)

“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)

Are you filling up your sin against God?

#4 They Face the Wrath of God (v16c)

"for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost"

In Ephesians 5 Paul gives a long list of common sins that people try to get away with. Then he writes in verse 6 "Let no man deceive you with vain words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience."

Are you facing the wrath of God?

You don't have to face God's wrath. You can be saved and forgiven! It all comes down to faith and belief.

"He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him." (John 3:36)

None of us should be God's enemy!

Please, DO NOT:

Fight the Power of God

Forbid the Word of God

Fill Up Sin Against God

Face the Wrath of God

title: Be A Paul!
body:
The example of Apostle Paul's life is one we should all follow, as he wrote "Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ." (1 Corinthians 11:1)

And I desire to pattern my ministry after that of Paul. We have his example of ministry all over the New Testament, and a few of his characteristics stand out in 1 Thessalonians 2:1-12.

He Was Confident In God's Power (v1-2)

Amidst suffering (v2a)

Amidst shame (v2b)

Amidst contention (v2c)

He Was Centered On God's Truth (v3-5)

Not on mischief (v3)

Not on man-pleasing (v4-5)

Not on money (v5)

He Was Committed To God's Love (v6-11)

He exhibited the humble love of God (v6)

He exhibited the nurturing love of God (v7)

He exhibited the sacrificial love of God (v8-9)

He exhibited the righteous love of God (v10)

He exhibited the authoritative love of God (v11)

All because he wanted folks to be saved and able to have a life "worthy of God who hath called you unto his kingdom and glory."! (v12)

title: My Kind Of Church!
body:
The church of the Thessalonians was my kind of church!

In 1 Thessalonians chapter 1 Paul recognized what kind of church they were:

They Were A Sincere Church! (1:1-3)

Work of faith (v3)

Labor of love (v3)

Patience of hope (v3)

They Were A Surrendered Church! (1:4-6)

They were chosen (v4)

They received the word (v6)

They repented (v9)

They followed the Lord (v6)

(They surrendered themselves to be like Christ!)

They Were A Sounding Out Church! (1:7-9)

Their LIVES sounded out and pointed people to Christ (v7)

Their WORDS sounded out and pointed people to Christ (v8)

"ensample" = pattern

"sounded out" = echo

They sounded out Christ (v8)

to the north (Macedonia)

to the south (Achaia)

"also in every place" (wherever they went!)

They Were A Second Coming Church! (verse10)

They were looking for Christ's return!

Jesus said "...I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself, that where I am, there ye may be also." (John 14:2,3)

The Church of the Thessalonians knew that people needed to come to Jesus now, because Jesus would be coming back soon!

"And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely." (Revelation 22:17)

"He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so come, Lord Jesus." (Rev 22:20)

A footnote about Flat Gap Baptist Church:

I am very grateful I get to serve in a church that is similar to that one at Thessalonica! There's always room for improvement, but WOW, what a church we have at Flat Gap Baptist!

A Sincere Church!

A Surrendered Church!

A Sounding Out Church!

A Second Coming Church!

title: Do You Stumble In Serving God?
body:
My #1 stumbling block that hinders me from doing what God wants is... me! I feel I'm not good enough, or I don't know enough. I'm just not sure enough, or think I can't do enough to be successful for God.

But then I'm reminded of 1 Corinthians 1:26-29.

"For you see your calling, brethern, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble are called: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence."

And verse 31 "That according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord."

In Exodous 3 and 4 we learn how God used Moses, even though Moses felt the same stumbling blocks I do. God answers our every stumbling block!

Stumbling Block #1: Lack of Self Esteem.

"Who am I?" (Exodous 3:11)

We should glory that God is with us! (Ex. 3:12)

Stumbling Block #2: Lack of Knowledge

Moses didn't know God's name. (Ex. 3:13)

We should glory that we know God, The Great I AM! (Ex. 3:14 & Jeremiah 9:23-24)

Stumbling Block #3: Lack of Confidence

"They will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice." (Ex. 4:1)

We should glory that God uses what we have!

"What is that in thine hand?" (Ex. 4:2)

Stumbling Block #4: Lack of Ability

"I am not eloquent...I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue." (Ex. 4:10)

We should glory in God's grace! (Ex. 4:11 & 2 Corinthians 12:9-10)

Moses succeeded and so will we! Not because of our own wisdom, or might, or riches, or of anything of ourselves. It's all God!

"That according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord."

title: Some Thoughts About Halloween
body:
While reading Ephesians 5:8-17, I am reminded of some aspects concerning Halloween.

During the Halloween season...

#1 Darkness is Enhanced

-but-

THE LIGHT OF CHRIST DISPELS DARKNESS!

(John 8:12)

#2 Evil is Exalted

-but-

THE GOODNESS OF CHRIST OVERCOMES EVIL!

(Romans 12:12)

#3 Sin is Expected

-but-

THE MANIFESTATION OF CHRIST DESTROYS SIN!

(1 John 3:8)

#4 Death is Exploited

-but-

THE VICTORY OF CHRIST DEFEATS DEATH!

(1 Cor 15:55-57)

#5 Fear is Embraced

-but-

THE LOVE OF CHRIST CASTS OUT FEAR!

(1 John 4:18)

"For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light" -Ephesians 5:8

title: Not Just A Fish Story
body:
There are some lessons to gain from the account of Peter with Jesus at Lake Gennesart in Luke 5:1-11:

I want to be faithful to God...

...when asked to do little things (v3)

...when it does not make sense (v4-5)

...when I need help (v6-7)

...when I feel unworthy (v8)

...when I'm astonished and afraid (v9-10)

...when Jesus calls! (v10-11)

Luke 5:1-11

title: Do You Want To Triumph?
body:
In 2 Corinthians 2:11-17 we see that there is Victory in Jesus even in the midst of despair and depression. Paul had "no rest in my spirit" in verse 13 and actually went away from "a door opened unto me of the Lord". But then his attention turned to Jesus!

Even when we don't feel great, God reminds us of the following truths:

We are Triumphant Winners in Christ! (v14)

We are Triumphant Witnesses for Christ! (v15-16)

We Share the Triumphant Words of Christ! (v17)

"Now thanks be unto God which always causeth us to triumph in Christ and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place" -2 Corinthians 2:14
